tenant-restrictions.title: Set up tenant restrictions v2 – Microsoft Learn
tenant-restrictions.notes: Tenant restrictions v2 is part of the cross-tenant access settings in Microsoft Entra External ID and lets an organization control which external accounts people may use on its networks and managed devices. The goal is to stop sign-ins with accounts from unknown tenants and to reduce data leaving through external identities. Authentication plane protection blocks sign-ins with external identities, while data plane protection, still in preview, also covers bypasses such as anonymous Teams meeting joins or anonymous SharePoint file access. It can be enforced through Global Secure Access, through a corporate proxy that injects a policy header on sign-in requests, or on Windows devices through group policy, where the Windows option is only partial. A default policy applies to everyone, and partner-specific policies can override it per tenant, user, group or application. Configuration requires Microsoft Entra ID P1 or P2 and at least the Security Administrator role. Known limits include no coverage of anonymous consumer OneDrive access and of tokens copied from a home machine to a work machine.

threat-analytics.title: Threat analytics in Microsoft Defender XDR – Microsoft Learn
threat-analytics.notes: Threat analytics is the built-in threat intelligence feature of the Microsoft Defender portal, written by Microsoft security researchers and complemented by curated OSINT articles. It covers active threat actors and their campaigns, attack techniques, critical vulnerabilities and common malware. The dashboard groups reports into latest threats, high-impact threats and highest exposure threats, and can be filtered by tags such as ransomware or phishing. Each report has sections for an overview, an analyst report with attack chains and hunting guidance, related incidents, impacted assets, endpoint exposure, recommended actions and indicators of compromise. Security teams use it to judge whether their organization is affected, to see which assets are touched and to prioritize mitigations. Access needs a license for at least one Defender product, though Defender for Endpoint Plan 1 does not grant it, plus suitable read roles for the underlying data. Recommended actions only draw on Secure Score, and the indicators section is a preview limited to verified customers.

time-entry-agent.title: Enable the Time Entry Agent – Microsoft Learn
time-entry-agent.notes: The Time Entry Agent is a production-ready preview feature of Dynamics 365 Project Operations that helps team members record their time entries. It applies to both Project Operations integrated with ERP and Project Operations Core, and it requires a minimum product version. The agent is built in Copilot Studio and works together with a set of Power Automate cloud flows delivered in the Project Service agent solution, which handle imports, duplicate filtering, adaptive cards and alerts for missing entries. An administrator turns on a feature flag in the project parameters, activates the flows, and publishes the agent. Users can reach it through an optional Teams app or directly from the time entry grid. A dedicated agent user is optional and needs a specific role, and the flows rely on Power Automate, Teams and Microsoft 365 E5 licensing for calendar access. Setup steps must be repeated for each environment, the flows have to be activated in a fixed order, and the page describes the agent's abilities only in general terms.

tmdl.title: Tabular Model Definition Language (TMDL) – Microsoft Learn
tmdl.notes: TMDL is a text syntax for defining objects in tabular data models that use compatibility level 1200 or higher. It exposes the same properties as the Tabular Object Model, so it maps fully to TOM. The grammar resembles YAML, with hierarchy expressed through indentation, which makes the files readable and easier to edit, including embedded DAX and M expressions. A model is stored as a folder in which each table, role, perspective and culture has its own file, while columns, hierarchies and partitions live inside their parent table file. Root files such as database, model, relationships, expressions and data sources complete the layout. This structure suits source control and collaborative work on Power BI semantic models. Developers can read and write the format through the TmdlSerializer class in the Tabular namespace. Limits include strict indentation rules that cause parsing errors when violated, a ban on declaring the same property in two documents, and the fact that the server object is not part of what TMDL represents.

token-protection.title: Token protection in Conditional Access – Microsoft Learn
token-protection.notes: Token protection is a Conditional Access session control that aims to reduce token replay attacks. When enabled, Microsoft Entra ID accepts only sign-in session tokens that are cryptographically bound to a device, such as a primary refresh token issued at device registration, when supported applications access protected resources. A stolen token is therefore not usable from another device. Native apps for Exchange Online, SharePoint Online and Teams are supported on Windows, iOS and macOS, with Azure Virtual Desktop and Windows 365 also covered on Windows. Browser-based access is a preview limited to selected web apps for Azure Resource Manager on Windows and macOS, and iOS does not support browser apps. Requirements include joined or registered Windows devices, or MDM-managed Apple devices with the Microsoft Enterprise SSO plug-in. Microsoft advises starting with a pilot group and report-only mode while reviewing sign-in logs. The page presents the feature as one layer of a defense-in-depth approach, not a complete safeguard, and lists no license requirements.

unattended-desktop-flow.title: Run unattended desktop flows – Microsoft Learn
unattended-desktop-flow.notes: Unattended desktop flows are Power Automate desktop flows that run without human supervision, typically triggered from cloud flows. A desktop flow connection signs in to the target machine automatically, runs the flow, then signs out and logs the activity. Power Automate creates an RDP session for the run, keeps the screen locked so nobody can watch, and releases the Windows user session afterwards. Console session access is not available for these runs. Sessions can optionally be reused after a run. Unattended automation requires the Power Automate Process plan, and the connection user needs permission to create an RDP session, usually through the Remote Desktop Users group. Sign-in with certificate-based authentication or network level authentication through Microsoft Entra ID requires admin consent for a specific remote desktop app ID. Limits include the need for a machine with signed-out users, no elevated privileges, no sign-in during a running flow, and no support for audio devices, cameras or webcams.

unified-routing.title: Overview of unified routing – Microsoft Learn
unified-routing.notes: Unified routing is a routing and assignment capability in Dynamics 365 that sends incoming work items to the best-suited queue and service representative by matching the work item's needs against representative skills. Its purpose is to connect customers with the right person, improve resolution at first contact and treat work consistently across channels, while taking a representative's engagement on other channels into account. Processing has two stages. Classification enriches a work item using rules and machine learning models, and assignment then prioritizes it and picks a representative based on work type, related entities, skills, availability and capacity. Further functions include skill-based routing, machine learning models that predict skills, and prioritization within a queue. Administrators configure it in the Copilot Service admin center, and representatives receive work through unified routing only when they use the Copilot Service workspace app. The intelligent skill finder depends on AI Builder availability and its supported languages. The feature is not supported in Unified Service Desk, and the page does not mention license requirements.

virtual-network-data-gateway.title: What is a virtual network (VNet) data gateway – Microsoft Learn
virtual-network-data-gateway.notes: A virtual network data gateway connects Azure and other data services to Microsoft Fabric and Power Platform without needing an on-premises data gateway. It communicates securely with the data source, runs queries and returns the results to the service. The gateway can be used with private endpoints so that traffic avoids public endpoints, supports Private Link scenarios, and also works with public endpoints in Azure, other clouds or on premises. It runs on fully managed hardware, audits traffic to the data source and isolates compute to guard against cross-tenant attacks. Supported workloads include Fabric Dataflow Gen2, data pipelines, copy jobs, mirroring, Power BI semantic models and paginated reports. It is available for P, F and A4 to A7 capacity SKUs, with larger F SKUs recommended. Limits include no support for Power BI dataflows and datamarts, no changes to the VNet's region, subscription or resource group after creation, and OAuth2 tokens that are not renewed automatically and can expire, causing credential errors.

virtual-network-peering.title: Virtual network peering – Microsoft Learn
virtual-network-peering.notes: Azure virtual network peering connects two or more virtual networks so that they behave like one network for connectivity purposes. Traffic between peered networks stays on the Microsoft backbone and needs no public internet, gateway or encryption. Regular peering links networks in one region, global peering spans regions, and subnet peering selects only some subnets. Latency between virtual machines in peered networks of the same region matches latency inside one network, and throughput depends on the VM size rather than on the peering. Peering works across subscriptions, Microsoft Entra tenants and regions, and can include classic networks. Gateway transit lets a peered network use another network's gateway, and user-defined routes allow service chaining through a virtual appliance. Network security groups can restrict access, since the default is full connectivity. Typical uses are hub-and-spoke designs and cross-region links. Limits include that global peering cannot reach a Basic Load Balancer frontend, and a small fee applies to traffic over a peering.

viva-amplify.title: Overview of Viva Amplify – Microsoft Learn
viva-amplify.notes: Viva Amplify is an app for communications teams and leaders who want to reach employees with their messages. It brings communication work together in one place so that executive, corporate and HR communicators can plan and send content from a single hub. Built-in writing assistance is meant to make messages clearer and more effective for employees. Content can be published to several channels at the same time, and campaigns are managed centrally. Reports on the effect of campaigns show how messages were received and used, which helps teams plan later communication. The app is available only as a web application. Users reach it by signing in to Microsoft 365 online and searching for Amplify or opening it from the app launcher under the communication category. The overview page links to separate articles for setup and for user training. It does not state license requirements, the specific publishing channels or technical limits.

web-resources.title: Web resources for model-driven apps – Microsoft Learn
web-resources.notes: Web resources are virtual files stored in the Microsoft Dataverse database and served through a unique URL. They extend model-driven apps, for example by adding client-side logic to forms or by customizing the site map and the application ribbon. Supported file types include HTML, CSS, JScript, XML, XSL, RESX and several image formats such as PNG, JPG, GIF, ICO and SVG. Because they are records, they can be created, retrieved and updated through standard data operations and travel as solution components between environments. A web resource can be referenced with a dedicated directive in ribbon or site map XML, opened with a client API method, or reached through a relative URL. Access happens only inside the security context of the Dataverse web application, so only licensed users with the needed privileges can use them. The maximum file size is controlled by an organization setting. They run only in the browser, so no type can behave like a server-side ASP.NET page, and embedding authenticated content in an iframe is not supported.

web-roles.title: Create web roles – Power Pages – Microsoft Learn
web-roles.notes: A web role in Power Pages is a collection of permissions that applies to the content of a site. Authenticated users need a web role to gain access to restricted tables, which are governed by table permissions, or to restricted pages, which are governed by page permissions. Web roles are created and assigned in the Portal Management app under the security area. Each role has a name, an associated website and an optional description, and it can be flagged as the authenticated users role or the anonymous users role. The authenticated users role serves as the default for signed-in users who hold no other role, whereas the anonymous users role applies to visitors who are not signed in and takes only table permissions into account. A site may have just one role of each default kind, but a user can hold several web roles. Users are assigned either from the role record or from the contact record. With the enhanced data model, assignment is possible only from the contact. The page names no license requirements.

windows-autopilot-device-preparation.title: Windows Autopilot Device Preparation overview – Microsoft Learn
windows-autopilot-device-preparation.notes: Windows Autopilot Device Preparation sets up new devices so that people can start working with them. Instead of re-imaging, it turns the Windows 11 installation preinstalled by the manufacturer into a ready-to-use state, so custom images and per-model drivers are not needed. A single profile holds deployment and out-of-box experience settings, and Intune adds the device to a predefined security group at enrollment time when a user signs in. Selected apps and PowerShell scripts, including line-of-business and Win32 apps, are installed during the setup phase, and the flow can be user-driven or automatic. Users get standard rights by default, and reporting shows status per device, app and script. Requirements include a current Windows 11 version, Microsoft Entra ID and Microsoft Entra join, which is the only supported join type. Only the apps and scripts chosen in the profile install during the setup phase, and group policies are not tracked while the deployment runs. Device association is not yet available in sovereign clouds.

windows-laps.title: Windows LAPS overview – Microsoft Learn
windows-laps.notes: Windows Local Administrator Password Solution, or Windows LAPS, is a Windows feature that automatically manages and backs up the password of a local administrator account on Microsoft Entra joined or Windows Server Active Directory joined devices. On domain controllers it can also handle the DSRM account password. The passwords are rotated regularly, stored securely and offered to authorized administrators for sign-in or recovery. Microsoft points out that identical local admin passwords across many machines enable lateral movement. Backup targets are Microsoft Entra ID or Active Directory, and the feature supports password history, optional encryption in Active Directory and role-based access in Entra. Configuration works through the configuration service provider, group policy or a legacy emulation mode, and a PowerShell module is included. It is free on supported Windows versions, and Entra backup needs at least Entra ID Free. A device can back up to only one target at a time, workplace-joined clients are unsupported, and the legacy emulation mode stores passwords unencrypted in Active Directory.

windows-recall.title: Recall overview – Windows AI – Microsoft Learn
windows-recall.notes: Recall is a Windows feature that helps people find content they have previously seen on their PC. Users can search with semantic hints or scroll through a timeline of past activity such as apps, documents and websites. It works from snapshots of the screen, supports a relaunch button that returns to the displayed content, and offers pausing, filtering of specific apps or websites, and storage management. It requires a Copilot+ PC and a recent Windows update, and users must opt in under privacy and security settings. Snapshots stay local, and the page names Secured-core PC, the Pluton security processor and Windows Hello enhanced sign-in security as protections. IT administrators can control it through a client management policy that decides whether Windows saves snapshots and analyzes activity. Developers can enable relaunching through the UserActivity API, temporarily block capture of their windows, and add data loss prevention labels. Arm64EC apps are not supported, and the page gives no license or storage figures.
